context:
Add plain-name extras as ALIASES first (w1), keeping all dataframe- names functional.
Then merge the 2 conflicting dual-extras (w2, w3) into unified extras. Then update
internal references to prefer plain names (w4-w7). Every intermediate state is valid:
the dataframe- names never break, they just become the less-preferred spelling.
Convenience groups (dataframe-pandas-family, dataframe-expression-family, dataframe-all)
are kept as-is - they are rarely typed by users and "dataframe-all" is semantically clear.
description:
The `dataframe-` prefix on pyproject.toml extras (e.g., `dataframe-dask` instead of `dask`)
creates a poor UX: users must know the prefix convention to install optional dependencies.
Running `uv sync --extra dask` fails with a confusing error - the correct incantation is
`uv sync --extra dataframe-dask`.

Investigation found the prefix serves no real purpose for any of the 7 DataFrame platforms:
- **5 platforms** (polars, pandas, dask, modin, cudf) have no SQL-mode counterpart at all.
- **DataFusion** has `datafusion` (SQL+pyarrow) and `dataframe-datafusion` (DataFrame only).
  The only difference is pyarrow - a lightweight transitive dep that both modes benefit from.
  Merge into one `datafusion` extra including pyarrow.
- **PySpark/Spark** has `spark` (pyspark>=4.0.1) and `dataframe-pyspark` (pyspark>=3.5.0).
  The >=4.0.1 floor on `spark` is unjustified - every other pyspark reference in pyproject.toml
  uses >=3.5.0 (cloud-spark groups, dataframe-all, test deps). The Spark SQL adapter uses
  standard SparkSession APIs available since 3.x. Align to pyspark>=3.5.0 for both.

This item adds plain-name extras, merges the 2 conflicting dual-extras into single extras,
and updates all references to prefer plain names.

anti_patterns.dont: batch all pyproject.toml changes into one commit
anti_patterns.instead: commit w1, w2, w3 separately with dry-run verification.
anti_patterns.why: a typo in extras can break all installs
